text: Which biosafety level (BSL) is required for handling agents such as Ebola, Marburg, and smallpox -- pathogens causing life-threatening disease with no available vaccine or treatment?
explanation: BSL-4 is reserved for agents like Ebola, Marburg, Lassa, and smallpox that pose a high risk of life-threatening disease with no vaccine or treatment, requiring a full-body positive-pressure suit or class III biosafety cabinet. BSL-1 covers minimal-risk agents like E. coli K-12, BSL-2 covers moderate-risk agents such as Salmonella, and BSL-3 covers serious inhalation risks like M. tuberculosis or SARS-CoV-2 -- all lower containment tiers than what these agents require.
